To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the GH-receptor gene is regulated by GH and other cytokines; 2) this regulation is dependent on a functional GH-receptor; 3) the mechanism of GH-receptor regulation involves transcriptional activation; and 4) the GH-receptors of the GH-dependent and -independent cell lines are differentially regulated by GH and the other cytokines.

the GH mutants, GH1-2, -3, -4, -5 and -6, are all capable of regulating GH receptor (GH-R) gene transcription, with the exception of GH5, and that the GH-R gene is not regulated by the GH mutants, GHI-2, -4 and -5.
the growth hormone (GH)-receptor gene is regulated by the GH mutant proteins, and that the mutant proteins have the ability to activate the GH-receptor gene in a dose-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in the control of growth hormone (GH)-receptor gene expression and GH action.
the regulation of the GH-receptor gene by different GH mutants.
the regulation of the GH receptor gene by the GH mutants and the mechanism by which the GH-receptor gene is regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of GH on the regulation of the human GH-receptor gene in a human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line is dependent on the type of the GH molecule.
the use of GH and IGF-I in the treatment of GH deficiency is safe and effective.
the effect of GH on the regulation of its own gene is mediated by the GH receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a novel mechanism by which GH regulates GH-receptor gene expression in a human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line.
the effect of GH and its mutant on GH-receptor (GHR) gene transcription in a hepatoma cell line is investigated.
our results indicate that the regulation of the human GH-receptor gene is complex and that the different GH mutants may exert their effects through different pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GH receptor (GHR) gene is a target for regulation by GH.
the effect of GH on the transcriptional activity of the GH receptor gene is not limited to the 5′-flanking region of this gene.
GH and IGF-I are important regulators of hepatic GH receptor expression.
